blocks.text: O Nabi ﷺ! Tell the prisoners in your hands (in your custody), "If Allaah is aware of any good (Imaan) in your hearts (because of which you would soon become Muslims), He shall grant you better than that (ransom) which was taken from you, and will forgive you.[^1]
He said further, "This money is better than that which was taken from me (as ransom) but I have no idea about the promise of forgiveness."[^2]
The Manner in which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Distributed Wealth
The Practice of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in this Regard and the Public Treasury during his Period as Khalifah

Hadhrat Sahl bin Abi Hathma and others reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Baytul Maal (public treasury) in Sunh. It was known to all and no one guarded it. When people voiced the concern that it should be guarded, he said, "None should fear about it." "Why not?" they asked. "Because it has a lock on it," was the simple reply.

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to distribute everything the Baytul Maal contained so that nothing remained. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) moved (from Sunh) to Madinah, he kept the Baytul Maal in the house he lived. Proceeds from the mines of the Qabiliyya and Juhayna tribes came to him. The mine of the Banu Sulaym was also opened during his Khilaafah, so the Zakaah came from there as well. Everything was kept in the Baytul Maal. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to convert this into gold and silver nuggets and give every hundred people a specified amount (which they shared between themselves). He was fair in his distribution and all received justly whether they were slaves or free people, men or women, young or old. He also used the money to purchase camels, horses and weapons for people proceeding in Jihaad. During one of the years, he bought warm woollen shawls from the rural areas and distributed them amongst the widows of Madinah during winter.
